dedupe_keys.name: forest vegetation and lidar satellite models of mesh radio network connectivity gotenna pro field experiment idaho

description: This open-access study measures and models how forest vegetation and topography affect the connectivity of mesh radio networks used for wildland firefighting and public safety. A field experiment ran one mobile and five stationary goTenna Pro mesh radios on 24 Public Land Survey System sections of about 260 ha in northern Idaho; the full network was connected only 32.6 percent of the time on average (range 0 to 90.5 percent) and the mobile radio was disconnected from all others 18.2 percent of the time. Dirichlet regression models using lidar and satellite metrics, lidar only or satellite only predicted six connectivity levels with RMSE of 0.101 to 0.314, and vegetation metrics mattered more than topography. Producer: Zimbelman and Keefe, published in PLOS ONE on 7 December 2022. Coverage: forested sites in northern Idaho. Access: free to read on the PLOS website; a model code or data link was not confirmed. Licence and cost: CC BY per OpenAlex, free. Caveats: one radio type and one region, and the models predict connectivity of small ad hoc networks, not operator infrastructure. Simulation uses: the fitted models help plan communications for emergency response by predicting mesh connectivity from remote sensing data. Related records: none found for this specific topic.
